prerequisites: Solid command of basic arithmetic operations, differential and integral calculus, and physical quantities and SI units.
Ability to handle Newtonian mechanics, force equilibria, and mechanical work in simple examples.
Successful completion of the StEOP (Study Introduction and Orientation Phase).

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental concepts, laws, and applications of thermodynamics.
Ability to recognize and solve thermodynamic problems.
Independently solve tasks with thermodynamic boundary conditions and understand the most important energy-related, ecological, and energy-economic boundary conditions for our society.
To concisely present basic thermodynamic concepts for understanding relevant engineering contexts.
To clearly explain fundamental concepts, laws, and applications of thermodynamics.
To reliably distinguish and purposefully solve thermodynamic problems.
To independently solve tasks with thermodynamic boundary conditions.
To coherently explain energy technology, ecological, and energy economic boundary conditions in a societal context.
To consistently represent thermal and caloric equations of state for pure substances.
To apply the First Law of Thermodynamics and explain it with suitable examples.
To apply and clearly explain the Second Law of Thermodynamics, including its relation to entropy and irreversibility.
To present the fundamentals of thermodynamic cycles in a structured manner.
To apply the fundamentals and mechanisms of technical heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation, heat transmission, heat exchanger theory) to typical problems.
To perform energy and exergy analyses for given systems.
To discuss solution approaches for thermodynamic problems.
To work on tasks within partner and group work as well as peer feedback.
To explain one's own solution and calculation approaches.
To discuss constructive peer feedback appreciatively.
To critically examine information and sources.
To systematically compare alternatives and solution paths in tasks.

syllabus_topics: Thermal and caloric equations of state for pure substances
Introduction to multi-component thermodynamics (basic laws, humid air, mixtures and combustion)
Thermodynamic processes for heating and cooling (refrigeration machines and heat pumps)
Thermodynamic processes for propulsion and power generation (steam power cycle, gas power cycle, internal combustion engines, solar energy utilization, fuel cell)
Introduction to technical heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation, heat transmission, heat exchanger theory)

assessment_methods.method: Written colloquia with calculation examples and theory questions
